15130-the-fugitive-blacksmith-or-events-.creator: Unknown
15130-the-fugitive-blacksmith-or-events-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I answer I have been induced to do so on account of the increasing disposition to overlook the fact, that THE SIN of slavery lies in the chattel principle, or relation. Especially have I felt anxious to save professing Christians, and my brethren in the ministry, from falling into a great mistake.

arxiv-2011-13847.title: Autonomous learning of multiple, context-dependent tasks
arxiv-2011-13847.creator: Vieri Giuliano Santucci, Davide Montella, Bruno Castro da Silva, Gianluca Baldassarre
arxiv-2011-13847.description: Abstract When facing the problem of autonomously learning multiple tasks with reinforcement learning systems, researchers typically focus on solutions where just one parameterised policy per task is sufficient to solve them. However, in complex environments presenting different contexts, the same task might need a set of different skills to be solved.

arxiv-2012-13798.title: A new class of generative classifiers based on staged tree models
arxiv-2012-13798.creator: \Name Federico Carli \Email carli@dima.unige.it, \Name Manuele Leonelli \Email manuele.leonelli@ie.edu, \Name Gherardo Varando \Email gherardo.varando@uv.es
arxiv-2012-13798.description: Abstract Generative models for classification use the joint probability distribution of the class variable and the features to construct a decision rule. Among generative models, Bayesian networks and naive Bayes classifiers are the most commonly used and provide a clear graphical representation of the relationship among all variables.

arxiv-2109-11454.title: Modulating internal transition kinetics in responsive macromolecules by collective crowding
arxiv-2109-11454.creator: Upayan Baul, Nils Göth, Michael Bley, Joachim Dzubiella
arxiv-2109-11454.description: Abstract Packing and crowding are used in biology as mechanisms to (self-)regulate internal molecular or cellular processes based on collective signalling. Here, we study how the transition kinetics of an internal ’switch’ of responsive macromolecules is modified collectively by their spatial packing.

arxiv-2304-00576.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics as an Alternative to the Planet Nine Hypothesis
arxiv-2304-00576.creator: Katherine Brown, Harsh Mathur
arxiv-2304-00576.description: Abstract A new class of Kuiper belt objects that lie beyond Neptune with semimajor axes greater than 250 astronomical units show orbital anomalies that have been interpreted as evidence for an undiscovered ninth planet. We show that a modified gravity theory known as MOND (Modified Newtonian Dynamics) provides an alternative explanation for the anomalies using the well-established secular approximation.

arxiv-2306-02464.title: Graviton Mass Bounds in Very Special Relativity from Binary Pulsar’s Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2306-02464.creator: Alessandro Santoni, Jorge Alfaro, Alex Soto
arxiv-2306-02464.description: Abstract In this work we study the gravitational radiation produced by a keplerian binary system within the context of Very Special Linear Gravity (VSLG), a novel theory of linearized gravity in the framework of Very Special Relativity (VSR) allowing for a gauge-invariant mass m g m_{g} of the graviton.

arxiv-2404-03488.title: Electronic transport, metal-insulator transition, and Wigner crystallization in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
arxiv-2404-03488.creator: Yi Huang, Sankar Das Sarma
arxiv-2404-03488.description: Abstract Two recent electronic transport experiments from Columbia University and Harvard University have reported record high mobility and low channel densities in flux-grown transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) WSe 2 monolayers [J. Pack, et al. , arXiv:2310.19782 [cond-mat.mes-hall]; A. Y. Joe, et al. , Phys. Rev. Lett. 132 , 056303 (2024) ].

arxiv-2405-11402.title: A Model for Optimal Resilient Planning Subject to Fallible Actuators
arxiv-2405-11402.creator: Kyle Baldes, Diptanil Chaudhuri, Jason M. O’Kane, Dylan A. Shell
arxiv-2405-11402.description: Abstract Robots incurring component failures ought to adapt their behavior to best realize still-attainable goals under reduced capacity. We formulate the problem of planning with actuators known a priori to be susceptible to failure within the Markov Decision Processes (MDP) framework.

arxiv-2408-06061.title: Quantum Algorithms for Compositional Text Processing
arxiv-2408-06061.creator: Tuomas Laakkonen, Konstantinos Meichanetzidis, Bob Coecke
arxiv-2408-06061.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tuomas Laakkonen, Konstantinos Meichanetzidis, Bob Coecke. Quantum computing and AI have found a fruitful intersection in the field of natural language processing. We focus on the recently proposed DisCoCirc framework for natural language, and propose a quantum adaptation, QDisCoCirc. This is motivated by a compositional approach to rendering AI interpretable: the behavior of the whole can be understood in terms of the behavior of parts, and the way they are put together.

arxiv-2412-08619.title: Physics Context Builders: A Modular Framework for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2412-08619.creator: Vahid Balazadeh, Mohammadmehdi Ataei, Hyunmin Cheong, Amir Hosein Khasahmadi, Rahul G. Krishnan
arxiv-2412-08619.description: Abstract Physical reasoning remains a significant challenge for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). This limitation arises from an inability to translate learned knowledge into predictions about physical behavior. Although continual fine-tuning can mitigate this issue, it is expensive for large models and impractical to perform repeatedly for every task.

arxiv-2505-19645.title: MoESD: Unveil Speculative Decoding’s Potential for Accelerating Sparse MoE
arxiv-2505-19645.creator: Zongle Huang, Lei Zhu, Zongyuan Zhan, Ting Hu, Weikai Mao, Xianzhi Yu, Yongpan Liu, Tianyu Zhang
arxiv-2505-19645.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across many applications, with Mixture of Experts (MoE) models demonstrating great potential. Compared to traditional dense models, MoEs achieve better performance with less computation. Speculative decoding (SD) is a widely used technique to accelerate LLM inference without accuracy loss, but it has been considered efficient only for dense models.

arxiv-2603-06738.title: Rank-Factorized Implicit Neural Bias: Scaling Super-Resolution Transformer with FlashAttention
arxiv-2603-06738.creator: Dongheon Lee, Seokju Yun, Jaegyun Im, Youngmin Ro

pmc-11609261.title: Exploring the spatial and spatiotemporal patterns of severe food insecurity across Africa (2015–2021)
pmc-11609261.creator: Mesfin M. Ayalew, Zelalem G. Dessie, Aweke A. Mitiku, Temesgen Zewotir
pmc-11609261.description: Food insecurity is a rapidly increasing global challenge. It has multiple adverse effects on public health and nutrition outcomes. The level and patterns of severe food insecurity vary by region. This study, therefore, aims to investigate the spatial and spatio-temporal patterns of severe food insecurity across the African continent.

pmc-11782560.title: Cross-modality fusion with EEG and text for enhanced emotion detection in English writing
pmc-11782560.creator: Jing Wang, Ci Zhang
pmc-11782560.description: IntroductionEmotion detection in written text is critical for applications in human-computer interaction, affective computing, and personalized content recommendation. Traditional approaches to emotion detection primarily leverage textual features, using natural language processing techniques such as sentiment analysis, which, while effective, may miss subtle nuances of emotions.

pmc-13068220.title: Association of visceral fat and plasmacytoid dendritic cell-derived interferon alpha with SARS-CoV-2 infection
pmc-13068220.creator: Naoki Ozato, Shota Hori, Nobuyuki Miyai, Hideto Takase, Ryohei Tsuji, Noriko Osaki, Daisuke Fujiwara, Mikio Arita
pmc-13068220.description: Type I interferon (IFN-I: IFNα/β) production by plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) is critical for controlling viral infections. Visceral fat obesity is associated with severe outcomes in viral infections, but its effect on pDC-mediated IFN-I production in the context of SARS-CoV-2 infection remains unclear.

pmc-13069076.title: First report of therapeutic investigation and metabolic profiling of edible mushroom Agaricus flocculosipes
pmc-13069076.creator: Divya Sreekala, Vipin Mohan Dan, Gama Mohan M. Geetha, Arya Chamaparambath, Anagha Bindu, Sajith Raghunandanan, Chittethu Kunjan Pradeep
pmc-13069076.description: The genus Agaricus, classified under the family Agaricaceae and order Agaricales of the class Basidiomycota, comprises nearly 500 species with a cosmopolitan distribution. This genus includes both edible and non-edible species, several of which hold significant nutritional and pharmacological value. Many of these edible mushrooms are well explored for their medicinal properties.

pmc-13342777.title: Rapid Human Skin Barrier Disruption by Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate and Associated Molecular Mechanisms
pmc-13342777.creator: Manru Li, Huseyn Babayev, Paolo D'Avino, Can Zeyneloğlu, Ceren Bicer, Duygu Yazici, Yagiz Pat, Per Svedenhag, Nicolas Gaudenzio, Cezmi A Akdis, Yasutaka Mitamura
pmc-13342777.description: BackgroundEpithelial barrier disruption is a hallmark of allergic skin diseases. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), a surfactant in household cleaning products, is known to impair the barrier.MethodsWe used a physiologically relevant ex vivo human skin combined with real‐time electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to monitor barrier integrity after SDS exposure. Multi‐omics analyses, including RNA sequencing and proximity extension‐based proteomics, characterized molecular responses.

pmc-13391373.title: Darkness and body size shaped end-Cretaceous marine extinction patterns
pmc-13391373.creator: Rui Ying, Fanny M Monteiro, James D Witts, Daniela N Schmidt
pmc-13391373.description: The Chicxulub asteroid impact at the Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) boundary (66 Ma) is thought to have caused the extinction of around 75% of species in the fossil record by triggering catastrophic environmental changes1. However, despite decades of research, the mechanisms linking the environmental changes to the selective extinction patterns observed in the marine fossil record remain unresolved.

pmc-13594509.title: Impact of Cipepofol versus Propofol on Long-Term Cardiovascular Outcomes After TAVR: An Extended Follow-Up of a Randomized Trial
pmc-13594509.creator: Tingting Ni, Yantian Lv, Laiying Zhou, Jing Yu, Xincheng Tao, Han Cao, Yuanyuan Yao, Min Yan
pmc-13594509.description: BackgroundPatients undergoing transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) under general anesthesia are particularly vulnerable to hemodynamic instability. General anesthesia remains a common approach and is necessary in selected patients, although conscious sedation is increasingly used. A previous randomized trial showed greater peri-induction hemodynamic stability with cipepofol than with propofol, but whether this translates into improved clinical outcomes is uncertain.
